title: How long are paraffin blocks and slides typically archived?
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: How long are paraffin blocks and slides typically archived?

title: In the TNM system, 'N' refers to:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: In the TNM system, 'N' refers to:
body.explanation: T = tumour size/extent, N = nodes, M = distant metastases.

title: Which is NOT a role of pathology listed in the lecture?
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Which is NOT a role of pathology listed in the lecture?
body.explanation: The four roles: diagnostic, prognostic, therapeutic response, research.

title: Oxygen at high concentration is listed as a:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Oxygen at high concentration is listed as a:
body.explanation: With cyanide, arsenic, mercury, acids, pollutants, pesticides, hypertonic solutions, alcohol and drugs.

title: Tissue macrophages are also called:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Tissue macrophages are also called:
body.explanation: Bone marrow monoblast → blood monocyte → tissue histiocyte.

title: Fibrinoid necrosis stains like:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Fibrinoid necrosis stains like:
body.explanation: Immune complexes plus fibrin in vessel walls in autoimmune disease.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:pathanat

title: Hypoxia drives tumour angiogenesis through:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Hypoxia drives tumour angiogenesis through:

title: Worldwide, cancer is which cause of death?
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Worldwide, cancer is which cause of death?
body.explanation: About 1.5 million new cases and over 500,000 deaths per year in the cited figures.

title: What is the main disadvantage of frozen section compared with paraffin sections?
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: What is the main disadvantage of frozen section compared with paraffin sections?
options: It cannot be done during surgery
body.explanation: Frozen sections are fast but the morphology is inferior to paraffin, so the diagnosis must be confirmed after formal fixation and embedding.

title: Pink frothy sputum with dyspnoea suggests:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Pink frothy sputum with dyspnoea suggests:
body.explanation: Fluid in the alveoli, usually from left heart failure or ARDS.

title: Which is an anti-inflammatory cytokine?
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Which is an anti-inflammatory cytokine?
body.explanation: IL-4, IL-10 and IL-13 are anti-inflammatory; IL-1, TNF-α and IL-6 are pro-inflammatory.

title: Which condition causes localised oedema?
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Which condition causes localised oedema?
body.explanation: Generalised oedema comes from heart, kidney or liver failure and hypoproteinaemia.

title: The word necrosis comes from the Greek for:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: The word necrosis comes from the Greek for:
body.explanation: Nekrosis = death.

title: Benign prostatic hyperplasia is mainly driven by which hormone?
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Benign prostatic hyperplasia is mainly driven by which hormone?
body.explanation: Androgens, specifically DHT, drive stromal growth in BPH; treatment includes alpha-blockers and 5-alpha-reductase inhibitors.

title: Screening can detect cancer at:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Screening can detect cancer at:
body.explanation: Pap smear, HPV/HBV testing, BRCA screening.

title: ALK rearrangement in lung adenocarcinoma can be demonstrated by:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: ALK rearrangement in lung adenocarcinoma can be demonstrated by:
body.explanation: Gene fusions such as ALK, RET, NTRK and FGFR are therapeutic targets.

title: Cytocentrifugation is used for:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Cytocentrifugation is used for:
body.explanation: Fixation, centrifugation and staining must be prompt to avoid autolysis.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Frozen section. Cryostat during surgery; rapid but lower quality, confirmed on paraffin.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Staining. H&E standard: haematoxylin blue nuclei, eosin pink cytoplasm; special stains on demand.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Dysplasia. Disordered growth with atypia; precancerous.

title: Squamous metaplasia of the cervix is:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Squamous metaplasia of the cervix is:
options: A mesenchymal change forming bone in the stroma
A change caused mainly by vitamin A deficiency
Always a malignant lesion needing hysterectomy
body.explanation: It can mimic HSIL but lacks nuclear abnormalities and is immunohistochemically negative for p16.

title: Capillaries have:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Capillaries have:
body.explanation: Ideal for exchange of diffusible substances.

title: Which stain is positive for epithelial mucin but negative for connective-tissue mucin?
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Which stain is positive for epithelial mucin but negative for connective-tissue mucin?
body.explanation: Epithelial mucin is PAS-positive; connective-tissue mucin is PAS-negative but colloidal-iron positive; both are Alcian blue positive.

title: Which of these is NOT a disorder of blood vessels listed in the lecture?
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Which of these is NOT a disorder of blood vessels listed in the lecture?
body.explanation: Also arteriosclerosis, hypertension, varicose veins, thrombophlebitis, lymphoedema, tumours.

title: Nitric oxide in inflammation is produced by:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Nitric oxide in inflammation is produced by:
body.explanation: It relaxes smooth muscle.

title: Barrett's oesophagus is an example of which adaptation?
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Barrett's oesophagus is an example of which adaptation?
body.explanation: Chronic acid/bile reflux drives replacement of squamous oesophageal epithelium by columnar/intestinal-type epithelium — metaplasia.

title: Hyaline droplets in proximal tubular cells result from:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Hyaline droplets in proximal tubular cells result from:
body.explanation: An intracellular hyaline change.

title: Which civilisation practised removal and examination of internal organs around 3000 BC?
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Which civilisation practised removal and examination of internal organs around 3000 BC?
body.explanation: Through the religious practice of mummification.

title: Basal cell carcinoma of the skin illustrates:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Basal cell carcinoma of the skin illustrates:
options: A mature teratoma of the skin
A benign tumour that never recurs
body.explanation: Malignant morphology but rarely metastasises.

title: Veins are predisposed to:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Veins are predisposed to:
body.explanation: They have larger lumens and less organised walls, with valves.

title: In the lecture's classification of chemical carcinogens, cyclophosphamide and nitrosoureas are:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: In the lecture's classification of chemical carcinogens, cyclophosphamide and nitrosoureas are:
body.explanation: The lecture classes alkylating anticancer drugs (cyclophosphamide, nitrosoureas) as direct-acting initiators; indirect-acting ones are hydrocarbons, aromatic amines/azo dyes and aflatoxin.
option_notes: Promoters (e.g. hormones, phorbol esters) are not mutagenic; these drugs are initiators.
Listed in the lecture as direct-acting alkylating anticancer drugs.
Viral oncoproteins are e.g. HPV E6/E7, not drugs.
Benzopyrene is an indirect-acting polycyclic hydrocarbon needing P-450 activation.

title: In necrosis the cytoplasm becomes more eosinophilic because:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: In necrosis the cytoplasm becomes more eosinophilic because:
options: The nucleus enlarges and releases eosinophilic DNA
RNA content increases and binds eosin
Eosin binds denatured proteins and basophilia is lost with decreased RNA
body.explanation: Denatured proteins bind eosin; lost RNA removes basophilia; lost glycogen gives a glassy look.

title: Anaplastic cells show:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Anaplastic cells show:
options: Uniform small nuclei with fine chromatin
A thick capsule around each nodule
body.explanation: 'Growing backwards' — no resemblance to the origin.

title: Glioblastoma secreting PDGF illustrates:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Glioblastoma secreting PDGF illustrates:
body.explanation: Self-sufficiency in growth signals.

title: Which feature distinguishes necrosis from apoptosis?
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Which feature distinguishes necrosis from apoptosis?
body.explanation: Necrosis leaks cellular contents and elicits inflammation; apoptosis does not.

title: Ewing sarcoma carries:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Ewing sarcoma carries:
body.explanation: A fusion gene encoding a chimeric transcription factor.

title: Which tissue is PERMANENT (unable to regenerate)?
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Which tissue is PERMANENT (unable to regenerate)?
body.explanation: Myocardial cells and CNS neurons cannot regenerate; liver is stable, skin and marrow are labile.

title: Which organelle detoxifies harmful substances and synthesises lipids?
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Which organelle detoxifies harmful substances and synthesises lipids?
body.explanation: Rough ER makes proteins; Golgi packages them; lysosomes digest waste.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: ATP depletion. Without oxygen mitochondria cannot make ATP; injury starts here.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Aetiology. The cause of disease: primary if known, idiopathic if unknown; genetic or acquired.

title: A tumour derived from a single initial cell is:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: A tumour derived from a single initial cell is:
body.explanation: Clonality is one of the tumour characteristics.

title: CagA is a gene of:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: CagA is a gene of:
body.explanation: It stimulates growth-factor pathways in gastric cells.

title: Cystic fibrosis illustrates:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Cystic fibrosis illustrates:
body.explanation: With catarrhal inflammation and mucin-secreting tumours.

title: Familial adenomatous polyposis is a precursor condition that:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Familial adenomatous polyposis is a precursor condition that:
body.explanation: Genetic conditions like FAP and xeroderma pigmentosum surely predispose; acquired lesions like colonic adenoma or cirrhosis may predispose.

title: Compensatory hyperplasia of the liver after partial resection begins:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Compensatory hyperplasia of the liver after partial resection begins:
options: Immediately and is complete within an hour
As early as about 12 hours later
body.explanation: Mitotic activity in remaining hepatocytes can begin as early as 12 hours post-resection, eventually restoring liver mass.

title: Endometrial breakdown during the menstrual cycle is an example of apoptosis due to:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Endometrial breakdown during the menstrual cycle is an example of apoptosis due to:
body.explanation: Involution of hormone-dependent tissue is physiological.

title: A fine-needle aspiration (FNA) of a thyroid nodule is an example of which type of specimen?
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: A fine-needle aspiration (FNA) of a thyroid nodule is an example of which type of specimen?
body.explanation: FNA/FNAC collects isolated cells, making it a cytological specimen, unlike a biopsy which contains cells and tissue architecture.

title: Tumour cells achieve limitless replication by:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Tumour cells achieve limitless replication by:
body.explanation: Telomerase extends telomeres, preventing checkpoint-driven senescence.

title: Cassette engraving mainly serves to:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Cassette engraving mainly serves to:
body.explanation: Manual marker or laser engraving prevents specimen mix-ups.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Irreversible injury. Severe or progressive stress beyond repair.

title: Which of these is an endogenous cause of inflammation?
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Which of these is an endogenous cause of inflammation?
body.explanation: Endogenous: vascular abnormalities, dysregulated immunity, physiological.

title: Cellular adaptations are important because:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Cellular adaptations are important because:
options: They only occur during embryonic life
They are rare and of little clinical value
They are common, and some precede neoplasia
They are always irreversible once started
body.explanation: Also because the nomenclature is used daily in clinical work.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Section cutting. Microtome sections of 3 to 5 microns floated on a warm water bath.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Intrinsic (mitochondrial) pathway. The most frequent; balance of BCL-2 versus Bax/Bak; converges on caspase 9.

title: In the pathologist's reasoning, clinical information is the equivalent of:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: In the pathologist's reasoning, clinical information is the equivalent of:
body.explanation: The semiology of cellular and tissue alterations is the equivalent of the physical examination.

title: The incubation period is best described as:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: The incubation period is best described as:
options: The time between exposure and appearance of symptoms
A morphological change in the tissue
The expected outcome of the disease
body.explanation: It belongs to pathogenesis — how the disease develops.

title: Complications of Barrett's oesophagus include:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Complications of Barrett's oesophagus include:
body.explanation: Hence close surveillance programmes.

title: Pleomorphic adenoma combines:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Pleomorphic adenoma combines:
body.explanation: Fibroadenoma: glands plus fibrous tissue.

title: Why are neutrophils early and short-lived?
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Why are neutrophils early and short-lived?
options: They are rare and must be recruited slowly
They cannot phagocytose, so they die quickly
They are numerous and fast, then die within 48 h
They live for months and act late
body.explanation: P- and E-selectins are rapidly induced on endothelium.

title: Which stain detects iron (haemosiderin) in tissue?
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Which stain detects iron (haemosiderin) in tissue?
body.explanation: Perls' Prussian blue reaction detects haemosiderin/iron.

title: What does 'pathogenesis' refer to?
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: What does 'pathogenesis' refer to?
options: The mechanism by which the cause produces disease
The treatment plan for the patient
body.explanation: Pathogenesis (pathos + genesis) is the mechanism/development of the disease process.

title: Carcinogenesis is defined as:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Carcinogenesis is defined as:
options: Non-lethal genetic damage acquired or inherited
Lethal genetic damage killing the cell
body.explanation: Lethal damage would kill the cell; non-lethal damage lets it proliferate.

title: Excess BCL-2 in follicular lymphoma leads to:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Excess BCL-2 in follicular lymphoma leads to:
body.explanation: BCL-2 is anti-apoptotic; its overexpression prevents Bax/Bak release and cell death.

title: The locoregional stage of a cancer corresponds to:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: The locoregional stage of a cancer corresponds to:
options: Invasion of adjacent organs and vessels
body.explanation: Stages: local (in situ), locoregional (invasive), generalisation (emboli), metastasis.

title: Which is a systematic (systemic) pathology topic rather than a general pathology topic?
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Which is a systematic (systemic) pathology topic rather than a general pathology topic?
body.explanation: Systematic pathology applies general mechanisms to organ systems.

title: The first step of angiogenesis is:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: The first step of angiogenesis is:
body.explanation: Then migration, proliferation as buds, maturation, periendothelial recruitment.

title: Paper archives are usually kept:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Paper archives are usually kept:
body.explanation: They ensure confidentiality and support follow-up, research and quality assurance.

title: Inflammatory oedema is mediated by:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Inflammatory oedema is mediated by:

title: Symptoms of generalised oedema include:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Symptoms of generalised oedema include:
body.explanation: Anasarca from organ failure or severe protein deficiency.

title: During margination, red cells occupy:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: During margination, red cells occupy:
options: The periphery, next to the endothelium
The centre of the intravascular column, in rouleaux
body.explanation: Leukocytes move to the periphery.

title: Testicular pseudotumoral tuberculosis is histologically:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Testicular pseudotumoral tuberculosis is histologically:
options: An adenocarcinoma of the rete testis
body.explanation: It mimics a neoplasm clinically and radiologically.

title: Which oedema is typically NON-pitting?
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Which oedema is typically NON-pitting?
body.explanation: Lymphoedema, lipoedema and myxoedema do not leave a persistent indentation.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Metastasis. Secondary implants at a distance; benign tumours cannot do this.

title: TNM staging is less applicable to:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: TNM staging is less applicable to:
body.explanation: It is designed for solid tumours.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Calcium overload. Calcium accumulates in the cytoplasm.

title: Xeroderma pigmentosum is a precursor condition that:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Xeroderma pigmentosum is a precursor condition that:
body.explanation: A genetic DNA-repair defect.

title: Chronic irritation from smoking classically causes which change in bronchial epithelium?
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Chronic irritation from smoking classically causes which change in bronchial epithelium?
body.explanation: Normal ciliated columnar bronchial epithelium is replaced by more resistant stratified squamous epithelium — losing mucociliary clearance and predisposing to squamous cell carcinoma if persistent.

title: The three types of hereditary cancer are:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: The three types of hereditary cancer are:
body.explanation: Genetic predisposition can be screened.

title: Adenomas rarely exceed:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Adenomas rarely exceed:
body.explanation: Usually small, solitary, encapsulated.

title: Amyloid deposition in the liver causes hepatocyte atrophy by:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Amyloid deposition in the liver causes hepatocyte atrophy by:
body.explanation: Pressure atrophy also occurs with a spinal-canal tumour compressing the cord and vertebrae.

title: Pulmonary hypoplasia and the testes in Klinefelter syndrome are examples of:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Pulmonary hypoplasia and the testes in Klinefelter syndrome are examples of:
body.explanation: Congenital underdevelopment; technically not the opposite of hyperplasia.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Tumour progression. Independent mutations create subclones with greater malignant potential.

title: The Philadelphia chromosome t(9;22) creates:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: The Philadelphia chromosome t(9;22) creates:
options: BCR-ABL fusion with tyrosine kinase activity
body.explanation: BCR-ABL drives chronic myeloid leukaemia.

title: Pancreatic tissue found in the gastric antrum is an example of:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Pancreatic tissue found in the gastric antrum is an example of:
body.explanation: Heterotopia is the presence of cells not normally found in that tissue — a non-tumoral lesion.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Cell death. Necrosis or apoptosis when injury becomes irreversible.

title: Grossing is performed by:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Grossing is performed by:
options: A physician and a technician in pairs
body.explanation: Biopsies are counted and measured; specimens are oriented, measured, weighed and the margins inked.

title: Mutation of a guardian gene:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Mutation of a guardian gene:
options: Accelerates the acquisition of other mutations
body.explanation: It removes the damage-control response.

title: Which step in tissue processing removes the fixative before clearing?
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Which step in tissue processing removes the fixative before clearing?
body.explanation: Dehydration passes the tissue through increasing alcohol concentrations to remove water/fixative before clearing and wax infiltration.

title: Margins of a surgical specimen are inked to:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Margins of a surgical specimen are inked to:
options: Speed up fixation of the specimen
body.explanation: Ink marks the surgical edge so that margin status can be assessed.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Initiation. Cellular aggression activates mast cells, which release histamine.

title: Teratomas develop from:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Teratomas develop from:
options: The blastema of a single embryonic organ
Pluripotent cells of the three germ layers
body.explanation: They contain fully developed tissues (hair, bone, muscle); 95% are mature/benign, mostly ovarian.

title: Thymic involution reduces the thymus in adulthood by about:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Thymic involution reduces the thymus in adulthood by about:
body.explanation: Lymphoid tissue is replaced by fat; T-cell production falls; genetically programmed.

title: In necrosis, cytoplasmic RNA loss causes:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: In necrosis, cytoplasmic RNA loss causes:
options: Loss of basophilia and increased eosinophilia
body.explanation: Eosin binds denatured proteins; glycogen loss adds a glassy look.

title: Which of these is NOT a typical indication for frozen section?
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Which of these is NOT a typical indication for frozen section?
body.explanation: Frozen section is reserved for results with an immediate impact on the operation, not for routine, non-urgent diagnosis.

title: Caseous necrosis is bordered by:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Caseous necrosis is bordered by:
body.explanation: Friable yellow-white debris with obliterated architecture, characteristic of tuberculosis.

title: A high growth fraction tumour (e.g. lymphoma, small-cell lung cancer) is best treated by:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: A high growth fraction tumour (e.g. lymphoma, small-cell lung cancer) is best treated by:
body.explanation: High GF tumours respond to chemo/radiation; low GF tumours (breast, colon) are treated by debulking.

title: Slow narrowing of a vessel by atherosclerosis leads to:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Slow narrowing of a vessel by atherosclerosis leads to:

title: Russell bodies represent:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Russell bodies represent:
options: Excess immunoglobulin in the rough ER of plasma cells
Reabsorbed protein in renal tubular cells
Mucin stored in intestinal goblet cells
body.explanation: Russell bodies are intracellular hyaline in plasma cells.

title: Which element is at the arrow?
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Which element is at the arrow?
body.explanation: The arrow points to: Metastasis. Micrometastases grow into macroscopic secondary tumours.

title: Cell injury typically begins with:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Cell injury typically begins with:
body.explanation: Without ATP the membrane pumps fail and calcium accumulates in the cytoplasm.

title: Osteosarcoma is recognised by:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Osteosarcoma is recognised by:
body.explanation: Arising in the bone cortex and extending outward.

title: Palbociclib is an example of:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Palbociclib is an example of:
body.explanation: Cyclins and CDKs drive the cycle; inhibiting them is a therapeutic strategy.

title: Cellular ageing (senescence) leads to:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Cellular ageing (senescence) leads to:
options: Impaired replication and repair, ultimately cell death
body.explanation: Culminating in death of the individual.

title: What best defines dysplasia?
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: What best defines dysplasia?
options: A fully reversible increase in organ size from more cells
Replacement of one mature cell type by another mature type
Complete absence of an organ from a developmental defect
Disordered cellular growth with loss of uniformity and polarity, often precancerous
body.explanation: Dysplasia shows abnormal variation in cell size/shape and loss of normal architectural orientation, and carries malignant potential.

title: Apoptosis and necrosis:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Apoptosis and necrosis:
options: Are the same process with two names
Can never occur in the same tissue
Can coexist, and apoptosis may progress to necrosis
body.explanation: Some pathological stimuli induce apoptosis that then becomes necrosis.

title: Neoplasm literally means:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Neoplasm literally means:
body.explanation: Excessive autonomous growth caused by genetic mutations.

title: Autolysis is:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Autolysis is:
options: Enzymatic self-digestion of cells, mostly post-mortem
Programmed cell death in living tissue
body.explanation: Autolysis is distinct from both necrosis and apoptosis.

title: The first step of extracellular matrix invasion is:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: The first step of extracellular matrix invasion is:
options: Loosening of tumour cells by loss of E-cadherin
body.explanation: Loss of intercellular binding precedes proteolysis, altered attachment and migration.

title: Dysplasia is confined to:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Dysplasia is confined to:
body.explanation: Architectural and cytological changes without invasion.

title: Promoters differ from initiators because they:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Promoters differ from initiators because they:
options: Are not mutagenic but drive proliferation
body.explanation: Initiation → promotion → progression.

title: Macular oedema is most commonly caused by:
subject: subj:pathanat

body.stem: Macular oedema is most commonly caused by:
body.explanation: Diabetic retinopathy and retinal vein occlusion cause fluid in the macula, blurring central vision.

title: p14/ARF is epigenetically silenced in:

Only the shape of cells under a microscope
Only the genes that cause disease

title: A tumour bank stores samples:

title: PTEN mutation in Cowden syndrome is an example of hyperplasia caused by:

They are only ever inherited in the germ line
Both alleles must be mutated to have an effect

title: Epigenetic changes are:

Reversible, heritable expression changes without mutation
Changes found only in virus-infected cells

subject: subj:pathanat

options: It is only needed when an autopsy is done
It replaces the need for a microscope
It is only used in research protocols
It links the lesion with the clinical picture
body.explanation: Diagnosis requires correlating morphological findings with the clinical picture.

title: Haemorrhagic inflammation of the adrenal glands in meningococcaemia is:

How far the tumour has spread
